claims.statement: Postconceptional age (PCA) may clarify how bed sharing, maternal smoking, and prematurity relate to Sudden Unexpected Infant Death (SUID) incidence.
claims.quote: We examined whether postconceptional age (PCA), the sum of gestational and postnatal age, clarifies how bed sharing, maternal smoking, and prematurity relate to SUID incidence.

claims.statement: The study used negative binomial regression with PCA as the developmental time variable.
claims.quote: We analyzed 13,013 SUID cases (2008–2019) from the National Center for Fatality Review and Prevention Case Reporting System, modeling incidence across PCA with population-adjusted negative binomial regression.

claims.statement: Bed sharing was more strongly associated with SUID incidence in an early developmental window (PCA <43 weeks) than a later one (PCA ≥47 weeks).
claims.quote: Bed sharing was more strongly associated with incidence in an early developmental window (PCA <43 weeks; IRR 6.45, 95% CI 3.14–13.23) than a later one (PCA ≥47 weeks; IRR 2.10, 95% CI 1.70–2.58)

claims.statement: Maternal smoking and prematurity showed the same pattern as bed sharing in relation to SUID incidence.
claims.quote: maternal smoking and prematurity showed the same pattern while remaining positively associated throughout

claims.statement: The association between bed sharing and SUID incidence was further amplified by maternal smoking in a later developmental window (PCA ≥47 weeks).
claims.quote: Bed sharing’s association with incidence was further amplified by maternal smoking in the late window (interaction IRR 1.57, 95% CI 1.19–2.08)

claims.statement: Associations between SUID and bed sharing, maternal smoking, and prematurity were similar in males and females.
claims.quote: associations were similar in males and females, indicating these effects are sex-independent

claims.statement: The prespecified PCA window (36-90 weeks) is to be checked against a count-stability criterion of at least 5 cases per week in each of four tracked subgroups.
claims.quote: Prespecified PCA window (36-90 weeks) checked against a count-stability criterion of at least 5 cases per week in each of 4 tracked subgroups

claims.statement: A sensitivity analysis is planned comparing the primary PCA window (36-90 weeks) with an upper-bound sensitivity analysis restricting the window to PCA 36-79 weeks.
claims.quote: Late-window incidence rate ratios at the primary PCA window (36-90 weeks) versus an upper-bound sensitivity analysis restricting the window to PCA 36-79 weeks

claims.statement: Interaction terms from the windowed negative binomial models will be analyzed.
claims.quote: Prespecified interaction terms from the windowed negative binomial models

claims.statement: Sex-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios will be provided for PCA, bed sharing, maternal smoking, and preterm birth.
claims.quote: Adjusted incidence rate ratios and P values for PCA, bed sharing, maternal smoking, and preterm birth in the early and late windowed negative binomial models, stratified by sex

claims.statement: Birthweight-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios for bed sharing will be analyzed.
claims.quote: Adjusted incidence rate ratios for bed sharing in low-birthweight and non-low-birthweight strata, and for the bed sharing by low-birthweight interaction

claims.statement: Smoking-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios will be provided.
claims.quote: Adjusted incidence rate ratios for bed sharing in maternal-smoking and non-smoking strata in the early and late windowed negative binomial models, and the share of deaths occurring before one month of age by bed-sharing and smoking status

claims.statement: A comparison will be made between a PCA axis fit and a chronological-age axis fit using negative binomial generalized additive models.
claims.quote: Deviance, log-likelihood, AIC, model degrees of freedom, and pseudo R-squared for the negative binomial generalized additive model fit separately on the PCA axis and the chronological-age axis
